author: high
claim: For A=(I-Q)^{-1}, one has A+A^{\mathsf T}=I; consequently w=Au is nonzero and satisfies HQw=w.
evidence: The hypothesis ker(I-Q)={0} makes A well-defined. Orthogonality gives I-Q^T=-Q^T(I-Q), hence A^T=(I-Q^T)^{-1}=-AQ. Since A(I-Q)=I, -AQ=I-A, proving A+A^T=I. Thus u^TAu=1/2. With w=Au, Qw=w-u and u^TQw=-1/2, so HQw=Qw-2u(u^TQw)=Qw+u=w. Also w is nonzero because A is invertible and u^Tu=1.
